page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, featuring an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores using hyper-threading. The system is provisioned with 64.0 GB of memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent with 0 GPUs, no local storage is bundled into the configuration, and baseline network throughput is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation shows a distinct divergence between single-threaded execution and multi-core aggregate throughput. Single-core processing metrics are low, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 925.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.49, and bottom-tier throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics perform in the median range. The instance produces a Geekbench multi-core score of 5662.0, a PassMark CPU mark of 13262.56, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 57.21 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains typical mid-tier throughput, sustaining uncached read speeds of 77.7 GB/sec and write speeds of 59.92 GB/sec on large data blocks.

Because of its balanced vCPU-to-RAM allocation, this server provides dependable resource density for multi-threaded workloads, though older core architecture creates bottlenecks in execution paths that rely heavily on single-thread performance or advanced vector instructions. Performance on medium-scale language models remains constrained, achieving 20.3 prompt tokens per second and 8.09 generation tokens per second on 7B models. The configuration is primarily matched for horizontally scaled environments, including standard web serving pipelines, Redis caching clusters, microservices, and general database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose KVM virtual instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor. The configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark analysis highlights a tradeoff between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities: single-core scores sit in the bottom tier (925.0 in Geekbench single-core), while multi-threaded metrics remain firmly in the median range, reaching 5662.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 13262.56 in PassMark CPU. High-throughput operations perform reliably, including Redis SET execution at 11.29 million ops/sec and static web serving at 7.81 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost-effective resource density for horizontally scaled multi-threaded tasks, enterprise application servers, memory caching tiers, and batch data processing, but is less suited for workloads requiring high single-core execution speed.
